shortcuts.altNumber: Alt + number isn't used either, on purpose: on Windows, Alt with the numeric keypad is how you type characters that aren't on the keyboard (Alt + 164 = ñ). Intercepting it breaks typing accented characters. To switch tabs there are Alt + ← and Alt + →.

statusLine.benefit: With the status line configured, this CLI's tabs show their status, the “waiting” bar when it asks for permission to use a tool, the context meter with the exact window, and how much of your quota is left. Without it there's no way to know: the CLI doesn't leave it in any other file.
statusLine.checkHint: The app also notices on its own within a couple of seconds.
statusLine.copyTitle: Copy the line to the clipboard
statusLine.mergeHint: Merge it with what the file below already has, without replacing it: if it already has braces, add only the <kbd>statusLine</kbd> key.
statusLine.planBenefit: With the status line configured, the bar above the conversation shows how much of your plan you've used in the 5-hour window and in the week, and when each one resets. The CLI doesn't leave this in any other file, and only publishes it for subscription plans.
statusLine.planNoFragment: The app's folder has characters that the shell interprets inside quotes ($, ` or "), and with them there's no line the CLI can run. Moving the configuration folder to a path without those characters fixes it.
statusLine.planReplaces: The CLI allows a single status line: this one replaces any other you have. And with a status line configured, the CLI stops showing some hints at its bottom, such as “esc to interrupt”.
statusLine.planScriptHint: It only saves the two limits and the session id, in the app's folder, and prints them as a short line at the bottom of the CLI. It doesn't save the folder, the transcript, the cost or the model, which the CLI also passes to it.
statusLine.runsEverywhere: With the line in place, every CLI session runs it, including the ones you open outside the app, and it needs <kbd>node</kbd> in the PATH.
statusLine.scriptHint: It only saves the status, model and tokens of each conversation, and how much of your quota is left, in the app's folder. It doesn't save your email, your plan or the cost, which the CLI also passes to it, and it doesn't print anything: the CLI's own line stays as it is.
